    Pricing Workbench user guide

    What the workbench is for, the data it needs, how to install and run it from the downloaded zip, which files you open, edit or leave alone, and how to analyse what it produces for a reinsurance tender.

    Every number in this guide is synthetic.

    The screenshots come from dry runs on a personal laptop with the synthetic TRAINING_TENDER that ships in the release (some screens show the earlier release numbers 0.0.5 and 0.0.6; the steps are the same in 1.0.0). All rates, exposure and quotes are made up, and the cedant and reinsurers are fictional. This guide is also in the release zip as USER_GUIDE.html.

    Cedant workbookMake the blank workbook; GC types the cedant's current rates into it.1_make_cedant_workbook
    Read it backThe tool checks the filled workbook and turns it into the expiring catalogue.2_read_cedant_workbook
    Tender templateThe template the reinsurers fill, with the expiring rates shown for reference.3_make_tender_template
    EvaluateGates, rate index on the Merit cuts, benefit value, treaty feed and the scorecard.4_run_evaluation

    Before step 1, the tender's structure can be set up or changed in Excel with the Spec Builder, using the optional steps 0a_make_spec_builder and 0b_read_spec_builder (chapter 9).

    01

    What the workbench is for

    Context · read once

    In a medical quota-share tender, the cedant's medical book is offered to reinsurers, who quote their own rates for the cedant's catalogue (base rates by age, gender and member type, per product, emirate, TPA and plan), quote riders such as dental, optical and maternity, and offer terms (commission, profit share, loss corridor, cap, share). Each reinsurer's rates are a full alternative catalogue, so they cannot be compared by eye: one quote can be cheaper for young singles and dearer for married women, or cheaper on one TPA and dearer on another.

    The workbench answers the broker's questions on one consistent basis: how much does each quote change the price of the cedant's actual portfolio, where does it change it, what does that do to the treaty result, and which option or panel should we recommend? It does so by pricing the expiring catalogue and every quote on the same lives, the cedant's own exposure from Merit, cell by cell.

    Where it sits

    CedantCatalogueCurrent rates, factors, riders, benefits
    MeritExposureLife-level extract: who is insured, where, on which plan
    This toolPricing WorkbenchTemplate, checks, re-pricing, index, scorecard
    ReinsurersQuotesFilled tender templates and terms
    OutputsTreaty tool + packTreaty scenarios, recommendation pack

    The catalogue and the quotes flow in through workbooks the workbench generates itself, so it always knows where every number sits. Merit is read only through its published output contract. The treaty tool receives a scenario file; the workbench does not change either tool.

    The questions it answers

    B2 · Rate index

    How much dearer or cheaper is each quote?

    Option premium ÷ expiring premium on the standard mix, overall and by product, emirate, TPA and plan.
    B1 · Benefit value

    Is each option richer or leaner?

    Benefit lines compared with expiring and valued as factors, giving a benefit-adjusted index.
    TreatyFeed

    What does it do to the treaty?

    Premium change and loss-ratio effect per treaty book, ready for the treaty tool.
    D · Scorecard

    Which option or panel do we recommend?

    Price, robustness, data quality and terms scored on agreed weights, with weight sensitivity.
    T · Templates

    What do we send, and is what came back valid?

    Generates the cedant workbook and the reinsurer template; reads quotes back with integrity checks.
    A · Benchmark

    Where does it sit against the market?

    Optional: market plans priced on the same mix and a gap register. Not used in the training tender.

    What it does not do

    • It does not set rates or recommend a price. It measures quotes against expiring on the cedant's own mix.
    • It does not re-adjudicate claims or project experience. Experience enters only as each treaty book's loss ratio.
    • It does not invent business rules. Anything it cannot map or price stops the run with a list (MappingRequired), rather than being defaulted silently.
    • Loadings, fees and underwriting rules are not carried in the cedant workbook; the comparison is on base rates at loading 0.

    Principles worth knowing

    • Same lives, same basis. Expiring and every quote are priced on identical Merit cells, so the index measures rate change, not portfolio change.
    • Gated. Each stage checks its inputs (chapter 11) and stops with the reason rather than producing a number on bad data.
    • Deterministic. The same inputs and release give byte-identical outputs, and the run manifest records a hash of every input. A run can be repeated and audited.
    • Data boundary. The release holds synthetic data only. Client data lives in your tender folder on the GC laptop and never goes to a reinsurer.
    02

    What you need: data requirements

    Per tender · gather before you start

    A tender run needs seven inputs. Most are produced once per tender; the mapping tables are usually reused from one tender of the same cedant to the next.

    InputWhat it must containSourceChecked by
    Tender structure

    inputs\cedant_filled.xlsx    		Every base rate at the nil co-pay reference, before the TPA factor; every factor (reference = 1.0); rider rates; the option each plan is sold with; benefit values.GC analyst types it from the cedant's catalogue into the step-1 workbookCedant read-back gate (step 2)

    Mapping tables

    Reinsurer quotes

    Things Merit does not carry

    Merit has no co-pay level, deductible, pharmacy limit, annual limit option or dental / optical rider per life. The workbench holds these at the reference option for both expiring and quotes, so they cancel out of the comparison (chapter 12). Their value is assessed separately in the benefit outputs. If the cedant later supplies per-policy option codes, they can be added as an exposure override.

    Quality checks before you run

    • The Merit extract and the cedant catalogue cover the same products, emirates and TPAs as the tender spec.
    • The snapshot date (run config) falls inside the latest underwriting year, so lives in force are counted.
    • Quotes are on the issued template: no inserted rows or columns, no renamed sheets.
    • Rates are on the same basis as the template (annual, per member, net or gross as the cover sheet says).
    • Merit version. The workbench accepts Merit contracts IP4-8 (Merit up to v7.4.0), IP4-9 (v7.5.0) and IP4-11 (v7.7.0 to v7.8.2). A run from Merit v7.6.x (IP4-10) also loads, with a warning that its contract is not pinned. From v7.7.0 Merit's main tables hold in-scope rows only (the cedant's scope register is already applied), so the workbench needs no scope filter. From v7.5.0, where Merit calculates the policy type itself, larger groups are labelled Group (previously Non-SME): add a Group row to segment_map.csv, or the coverage check stops with MappingRequired.
    03

    Install (once per laptop)

    About 15 minutes

    • Windows with Python 3.12 (64-bit) and the py launcher (the team's standard runtime).
    • The pinned packages in requirements-native.txt (DuckDB, pandas, numpy, pyarrow, openpyxl, xlsxwriter and helpers), from GC Artifactory.
    • Microsoft Excel to fill the cedant workbook and read the outputs.

    Check Python in a Command Prompt:

    Command Prompt
    py -3.12 --version

    After unzipping (chapter 4), install the packages from inside the inner pricing-workbench-<version> folder (in File Explorer, click the address bar, type cmd, press Enter):

    Command Prompt, in pricing-workbench-<version>
    py -3.12 -m pip install -r requirements-native.txt

    The laptop check (chapter 6) reports any package that is missing or at the wrong version.

    04

    Download and unzip

    Every new release · 2 minutes

    Save the release zip into any folder you like; the tool does not care where it lives. Keep the path short (for example C:\pw, or a folder directly under Downloads or Documents) because Windows limits full paths to 260 characters.

    Do not run anything from inside the zip.

    Windows lets you browse into a zip, but programs started there cannot find their other files. Always extract first.

    1

    Put the zip in your folder and extract it

    Select the zip, click Extract all in the toolbar (or right-click, Extract All…), keep the suggested destination and click Extract.

    2

    Check what you got

    The extracted folder is your working area. It holds five things:

    • pricing-workbench-1.0.0: the tool itself. You never edit it.
    • USER_GUIDE.html: this guide. Open it in any browser; it works offline.
    • TENDER_TEMPLATE: a blank tender folder to copy for each real tender.
    • TRAINING_TENDER: a complete synthetic tender to practise on.
    • RUN_LAPTOP_CHECK.bat: the acceptance check for this release.
    Tender folders must sit next to the tool folder.

    Each step file looks for a pricing-workbench-* folder beside its own tender folder. Keep your tender folders in the working area. When a new release arrives, extract it to a new working area and copy your tender folders across. If two pricing-workbench-* folders sit side by side, the step files use the last one in name order, so keep one per working area.

    05

    Folder map: what to open, edit or leave alone

    Reference · click any folder or file

    In a normal tender you only double-click the step files, edit the inputs in your tender folder, and open the outputs. Everything inside the tool folder is code, tests and reference data.

    RUN double-click it EDIT you fill or replace it READ open it to read the results LEAVE do not touch

    Rules of thumb

    • Never edit the tool folder. A new release replaces it completely.
    • One tender, one folder. Inputs, the files the tool writes and the run results all live in the tender folder. Copy the whole folder to keep or move a tender.
    • A real tender folder holds client data. Keep it on the GC laptop. Reinsurers receive only work\tender_template.xlsx.
    • work\ and runs\ are rewritten each time a step runs. Save anything you change under a new name or in inputs\.
    06

    Run the laptop check

    Every new release · 20 to 30 minutes

    The laptop check proves that this release works on this laptop before you use it on a tender. It checks Python and every package version, confirms the release contents (including both tender folders), runs the full test suite, runs every tool once, runs the four steps of the training tender, runs a complete evaluation twice and compares the outputs byte for byte, and opens the generated workbooks in Excel.

    1

    Double-click RUN_LAPTOP_CHECK.bat once

    A window opens and results appear line by line as each check finishes. The test-suite step takes 10 to 25 minutes with no new lines, which is normal. Leave Excel alone while it runs, because the check opens and closes Excel itself.

    2

    If you double-click it again

    Only one check runs at a time. A second start says another check is running, exits with code 3 and changes nothing. Close that window and let the first one finish.

    3

    Read the last line and send it back

    The window ends with LAPTOP CHECK PASS or LAPTOP CHECK FAIL (n of m). The same text is in laptop_check_console.txt beside the batch file, and a fuller report in pricing-workbench-<version>\runs\laptop_check\<date-time>\laptop_check_report.md. Send the line, or the console file, to the tool owner.

    Why this screenshot says FAIL (48 of 49)

    The dry run was on a personal laptop with Python 3.14, so the one failed line is the Python 3.12 version check. Every package, every test, every tool, the training tender's four steps and the byte-identical rerun passed. On a GC laptop with the standard Python 3.12 the same release reads LAPTOP CHECK PASS. The 3 SKIP lines check files that are deliberately not shipped in a release.

    07

    Practice run: the training tender

    First time only · about 3 minutes

    TRAINING_TENDER is a complete tender on synthetic data: a fictional cedant's catalogue already typed into the cedant workbook, a synthetic Merit extract with its mapping tables, two fictional reinsurer quotes and treaty inputs. Run its four steps once before you touch client data, so you have seen every window and every output.

    Open TRAINING_TENDER and double-click the step files in order. Each window shows the command it runs and ends with DONE - exit code 0; press a key to close it.

    Then open runs\TRAINING\out\ and follow chapter 12 with the training results. In the training run, SUB_Y ranks first: it is about 0.8% cheaper than expiring on the standard mix (index 0.9923), while SUB_X is about 2.6% dearer (1.0255).

    08

    Set up a real tender

    Once per tender

    Timeline of a tender

    1. Get the tender structure. The tool owner writes template_spec.json from the cedant's catalogue (structure only).
    2. Copy TENDER_TEMPLATE in the working area and rename it (for example CEDANT_MEDQS_2027; any name works). Put the spec in inputs\.
    3. Step 1, then fill the cedant workbook from the cedant's catalogue and save it as inputs\cedant_filled.xlsx.
    4. Step 2 until it says CEDANT READ PASS.
    5. Step 3, then issue work\tender_template.xlsx to the reinsurers. Keep the exact copy you sent.
    6. While quotes are out: put the Merit extract and mapping tables in exposure\, the treaty inputs in treaty\, and edit run_config.json.
    7. When quotes return: save each in submissions\, add it to run_config.json, fill terms_scores.csv, and run step 4.
    8. Analyse (chapter 12), adjust panels or weights if agreed, and re-run step 4. Each run is repeatable.

    The run config

    Open run_config.json in Notepad and replace every CHANGE_ME. Paths are relative to the run config file; use forward slashes.

    SettingWhat it controls
    run_idName of the results folder runs\<run_id>\.
    exposure.snapshot_dateIn-force date for the standard mix: lives covered on this date in the latest underwriting year.
    treaty.lapse, book_slotsLapse assumed per treaty book in the treaty feed; the treaty tool slot (1 to 8) each book goes to.
    v5.outlier_bandQuoted ÷ expiring outside this band (default 0.7 to 1.3) is flagged.
    submissionsOne entry per quote: option_id (short code used in every output), owner, file, the spec and the issued template.
    gates.coverage_thresholdMinimum share of written premium that must map to a priced or referred cell (default 0.95).
    b2.basisMERIT_CUTS (default): compare on base + maternity at reference options. FULL: all options at catalogue defaults.
    scorecard.panelsPanels to score as one option, e.g. {"panel_id": "PANEL_AB", "lead": "RE_A", "members": {"RE_A": 0.6, "RE_B": 0.4}}.
    scorecard.show_reinsurer_names, market_facing, incumbent_namesWhat the pack shows. A market-facing pack never names the incumbent.

    Filling the cedant workbook

    SheetEnter
    Rate sheetsAnnual premium per member in every yellow cell: the nil co-pay base at the reference options under the sheet title, before the TPA factor. Grey cells are referred.
    FactorsOne factor per option; the Reference = Y row reads 1.0 (another value is kept and warned).
    RidersRider premium per limit, in the unit shown (per member; per eligible female for maternity).
    Plan defaultsThe option each plan is sold with. For riders, NONE = not purchased.
    BenefitsValue and source wording per benefit line. A blank row means the line does not apply. Fill them: the benefit outputs compare these lines.
    Never type co-pay variants.

    Where the source shows Nil / 10% / 20% blocks side by side, enter only the Nil block and the block multipliers as a factor table (Nil = 1.0). The tool generates the variants.

    What reinsurers receive and return

    09

    The tender structure: template_spec.json

    Once per tender · written by the tool owner, reviewed by the analyst

    What it is for

    template_spec.json describes the shape of one tender, and nothing else: which products and emirates are tendered, which TPAs price each one, which plans and networks each TPA has, the age bands and rate columns, which cells are referred, the reference options the base rates assume, and the factor tables, riders, plan defaults and benefit lines of the cedant's catalogue. It holds no rates and no client values.

    Every workbook in the tender is built from it, and every workbook is read back through it:

    Used byWhat the spec decides there
    Step 1: cedant workbookThe rate sheets and blocks GC fills, plus the Factors, Riders, Plan defaults and Benefits sheets with their rows already listed.
    Step 2: cedant read-backWhat a complete workbook looks like: every yellow cell it must find, one reference row per factor key, the allowed options for each plan default.
    Step 3: tender templateThe exact sheets, blocks, rows and columns the reinsurers fill, the Existing Rates and Factor Tables reference sheets, whether riders are quotable, and the Terms sheet.
    Step 4: quotes and gatesThe structure hash printed by step 3 is a fingerprint of the layout (every quote cell's key and position, the rate sheet names and the tender ID; not values, dates or Cover text). V5 accepts a quote only if it carries the issued hash, and V4 regenerates the template from the spec to prove generator and parser agree.

    Because one file drives all of this, the cedant workbook, the reinsurer template and the parser can never disagree about where a number belongs. The spec is the tender's contract with the tool.

    Freeze it before you issue.

    Once the tender template has gone to reinsurers, do not change the spec. Any change to blocks, plans, bands, columns or refer cells changes the structure hash, and quotes on the old template will fail V5. If a change is unavoidable, regenerate (steps 1 to 3), re-issue, and point issued in the run config at the new template.

    How the tender is laid out

    The spec follows the owner's template principle:

    • One sheet per product × emirate (e.g. Individual Dubai & NE, SME Abu Dhabi, a basic or compulsory plan).
    • One block per TPA on that sheet. A TPA appears at most once per sheet, even if the cedant's source shares one table between two TPAs.
    • Inside a block: one column group per plan (each plan carries its network for that TPA), rows by age band (or by member section, or by member category for simple plans), and columns by gender, gender × marital, or a single rate.
    • The base is the nil / 0% co-pay rate before the TPA factor. Co-pay, deductible, annual limit, network-option, nationality and TPA effects are separate factor tables, never extra blocks.

    Anatomy

    Top level

    FieldMeaning
    cedant, tender_idNames shown on every workbook's Cover. Required.
    currency, premium_basise.g. AED, NET or GROSS. Required. A sheet can state its own basis (premium_basis on the sheet) where the source differs.
    deadline, contact, issue_date, effective_dateShown on the tender template's Cover.
    age_band_sets or age_bands_fileNamed lists of bands, each {"label": "30-34", "range": [30, 34]}. Ranges may not overlap. A file (e.g. age_bands.json beside the spec) keeps long band lists out of the spec.
    column_setsNamed column layouts. Built in: MF (Male, Female) and RATE (one rate). Define others, e.g. MSF_MF: "M/SF" = male or single female, "Married-F" = married female.
    sheetsThe list of rate sheets (below). Required.
    reference_sheetsWhich reference sheets the tender template carries: existing_rates, factor_tables, addons (READ_ONLY or FILL, i.e. reinsurers quote riders; a blank rider cell means not quoted), tob_summary, terms.
    optionsprotect_structure, rounding, allow_benefit_comments, allow_proposed_multipliers, outlier_shading, language.
    cedant_workbookCedant-workbook settings: catalogue_id and version of the source catalogue, spare_rows (blank rows under each long table), notes (printed on its Cover: source flags, what to type where).

    Each sheet

    FieldMeaning
    sheet_name, titleTab name (1 to 31 characters, no []*?/\:) and the title printed on the sheet.
    product_type, regulator, rating_regionRegistry codes, e.g. INDIVIDUAL / SME / BASIC / NE_COMPULSORY; DHA / DOH / MOH_NE; the emirate code used in the exposure maps.
    age_bands or sections or rowsThe rows of every block: one band set; or sections, each with its own key and band set (e.g. Employee without an under-18 row, Dependant with one); or explicit rows for simple tables (e.g. member category × 0–64 / 65+).
    column_setThe column layout (default MF).
    split_optionsOptional extra splits a block can switch on: marital (use another column set, e.g. M/SF + Married-F) and member_section (sections).
    copay_basisThe reference options the base rates assume, e.g. {"copay_op_diag": "0%", "copay_pharmacy": "0%", "ded_consult": "20% up to AED 50"}. Printed under the sheet title so everyone prices the same base.
    mandatoryWhether every non-referred cell must be filled.
    refer_textThe text in referred cells (default "REFER - lead reinsurer").
    blocksOne per TPA (below).

    Each block (one TPA)

    FieldMeaning
    block_id, tpa, labelA unique id, the TPA code (as in tpa_map.csv), and the heading shown.
    plansEach {"plan_id", "label", "network"}: the plan code (as in plan_map.csv), the column heading, and the network of this plan for this TPA. The count is free: one TPA can have seven plans, another three.
    refer_cellsPartial keys of cells that are referred, not priced, e.g. {"plan": "P6", "age": [70, 120]}. They show grey with the refer text.
    splitsSwitch the sheet's split options on for this block, e.g. {"marital": true, "member_section": true}.
    overridesA block may set its own age_bands, sections, rows or column_set where it differs from the sheet.

    The cedant sections (per sheet)

    These sections tell step 1 which long tables to lay out for GC to fill. They list options and keys only; the values are typed into the cedant workbook.

    FieldMeaning
    scope_idThe id of the read-back scope for this sheet (e.g. IND_DXBNE).
    factor_tablesEach table: family (registry family, e.g. copay_op_diag, ded_consult, aml, copay_ip, tpa), its options, an optional key_dim with key_values when the factor varies by network, plan or TPA, the reference option (factor 1.0; one per key, or a {key: option} map), and tpas when the table applies to only some TPAs.
    ridersEach rider: family (module_dental, module_optical, module_maternity, …), the limit options, key_dim / key_values (e.g. by plan), the unit (PER_MEMBER, PER_ELIGIBLE_FEMALE, PER_FAMILY), the mode (ADD a premium or MULTIPLY the base), and optional key_labels telling GC which source column a key takes.
    plan_defaultsThe families for which GC records the option each plan is sold with (e.g. its standard co-pay or annual limit). It is used where Merit does not carry the option, and for riders NONE means not purchased.
    benefitsBenefit codes from the registry (aml, room_type, pec_waiting, dental_limit, …), optionally restricted to some plans: the rows of the Benefits sheet.
    premium_basis, formulaOptional: this sheet's own premium basis, and the order and rounding of the price build-up (default base, then factors, then riders).

    A worked example (fictional)

    One sheet, Individual in one emirate, two TPAs. The first TPA has three plans; the second has two, with different networks. Rates are by 5-year band and gender, ages 70+ on the lowest plan are referred, and there is one co-pay factor table and one maternity rider:

 }]
}

    From this, step 1 reports 148 rate cells, 2 refer cells, 3 factor rows, 6 rider rows, 6 plan defaults, 7 benefit rows: TPA A has 3 plans × 2 genders × 15 bands = 90 cells less the 2 referred (plan 3, 70+), TPA B has 2 × 2 × 15 = 60; the Factors sheet lists 0%, 10% and 20% with 0% as reference; the Riders sheet lists 3 plans × 2 limits; Plan defaults asks for the co-pay and maternity option of each of the 3 plans; and the Benefits sheet has the annual limit and room type for every plan plus the dental limit for plan 1. Step 3 produces the same blocks for the reinsurers, a quotable Add-ons sheet and a Terms sheet. The complete synthetic spec of the training tender is in TRAINING_TENDER\inputs\template_spec.json; open it in Notepad for a full working example.

    How it is set up

    1. Read the cedant's catalogue for structure. From its rate tables and table of benefits, list:
      • the products and emirates;
      • the TPAs on each, and each TPA's plans with their networks;
      • the age bands, and whether rates split by gender, marital status (married female including maternity), or member type (employee, dependant, investor, …);
      • which cells the cedant refers rather than prices;
      • the reference options the base assumes (the nil / 0% co-pay block);
      • every factor table, with its options and reference, and whether it varies by network, plan or TPA;
      • riders, with their limits, unit and how a plan picks its column;
      • the option each plan is sold with;
      • the benefit lines to compare.
      Note anything irregular in the source (shared tables, swapped labels, flat multipliers, erroneous cells) as a note on the cedant workbook's Cover.
    2. Write the spec. There are three routes.
      • In Excel, with the Spec Builder (the usual route; no JSON or Python): steps 0a and 0b, described in the next section.
      • By hand, from the listing above, as was done for the first tender. Start from the training spec or the example above.
      • From an existing catalogue spec, if the cedant's workbook has already been mapped into a catalogue:
        Command Prompt, in pricing-workbench-<version>
        py -3.12 tools\pw.py t generate --from-catalogue <catalogue spec.json> --tender tender.json --out-spec template_spec.json --out template.xlsx
        tender.json holds cedant, tender_id, deadline, contact and issue_date. This writes the sheets, blocks, plans, bands, columns and refer cells; add the cedant sections (factor tables, riders, plan defaults, benefits) and reference_sheets by hand.
      Codes must match the registries and the exposure maps: product, regulator and benefit codes come from the registry, and TPA and plan codes must be the ones tpa_map.csv and plan_map.csv map Merit's labels to.
    3. Validate it with step 1. Put it in inputs\ and run 1_make_cedant_workbook.bat. If anything is inconsistent, step 1 stops and lists every problem (see the table below). When it passes, it prints the counts: rate cells, refer cells, factor rows, rider rows, plan defaults and benefit rows.
    4. Review the blank cedant workbook against the catalogue, sheet by sheet: every TPA block, every plan and network, every age band, the column split, the grey referred cells, the reference basis under each title, every factor option and its reference, every rider limit. This is the moment to catch a missing plan or a wrong band, before anyone types rates.
    5. Check the reinsurer view. After GC has filled the cedant workbook and step 2 passes, run step 3 and look at the tender template the way a reinsurer will: the Cover, each rate sheet, Factor Tables, Add-ons and Terms.
    6. Freeze and issue. Keep the spec, the issued template and its structure hash together in the tender folder. From here on the spec does not change.

    Setting it up in Excel: the Spec Builder

    The Spec Builder is an Excel view of template_spec.json: dropdowns and yellow cells instead of JSON. The JSON stays the master. The tool reads the builder back into the JSON, and every step after it uses the JSON.

    1. Make the builder. Double-click 0a_make_spec_builder.bat. It writes work\spec_builder.xlsx, pre-filled from inputs\template_spec.json, or blank when there is none.
    2. Fill or change it and save it as inputs\spec_builder.xlsx. Yellow cells are inputs (* = mandatory); grey cells are information.
    3. Read it back. Double-click 0b_read_spec_builder.bat.
      • SPEC READ PASS writes inputs\template_spec.json. The previous one is kept as template_spec.previous.json.
      • SPEC READ FAIL lists each problem with its sheet and cell (e.g. Blocks!G7 age band set 'X' is not defined) and leaves the spec untouched. The full list is in inputs\template_spec_read_report.csv. Fix the cells and run 0b again.
    4. Check the result with steps 1 and 3, as in the list above.

    You can fix and re-read the same builder as often as needed, also after a PASS. If someone else changes template_spec.json after your builder was made, step 0b stops (spec_changed): make a new builder with 0a and copy your changes into it, so nobody's edit is lost.

    SheetOne row perNotes
    TenderfieldCedant, tender id, currency, basis, dates, contact; the reference sheets shown to reinsurers; options. Blank = the tool's default.
    ListsvalueDropdown sources for TPAs, rating regions, networks, band sets and column sets. Add a new name here first. Not read back.
    Age bandsbandBand set, label, age from, age to (open top band: to 120). Source "file …" = kept in the age bands file: edit that file, not these rows.
    Columnscolumn keyTwo rows with the same set and label make one column (e.g. M/SF = male, and single female). MF and RATE are built in.
    Sheetsrate sheetProduct × emirate: name (max 31 characters), title, product, regulator, rating region, row source, column set, refer text, formula.
    Co-pay basisfamilyThe basis the base rates are quoted at (e.g. copay_op_diag = 0%).
    Blocks / PlansTPA block / planBlock id, TPA, label, splits, overrides; then each block's plans with the TPA's network label, in column order.
    Sections / Custom rows / Refer cellssection / row key / ruleThe structured fields below.
    Factor tables / Riders / Optionstable / rider / optionCedant workbook tables; their options and the reference option (Reference = Y, one per key) are on Options.
    Plan defaults / Benefits / Cedant workbook / Cedant notesfamily / code / field / noteWhat the cedant workbook asks per plan, and its Cover.

    The structured fields.

    • Formula (Sheets): how the cedant's premium is built at read-back. BASE, FACTORS, MODULES (base × factors, then riders) or BASE, MODULES, FACTORS; blank = default.
    • Splits (Blocks: Marital split, Member split = Y): the block uses the sheet's Marital split columns and its Member split sections.
    • Sections: row sections with their own member category and band set. Applies to = Sheet rows, Member split, or a block id.
    • Custom rows: hand-built rows for irregular tables; two lines with the same row label and section make one row covering both keys (e.g. 00-64 Employee & Dependants). One row source per sheet or block: a band set, sections or custom rows.
    • Refer cells: cells reinsurers do not quote. Blank = any; a cell matching every filled field is a refer cell (e.g. Member category PARENT = the whole parents row).
    Typing text that looks like a number or date.

    Excel turns 10% into 0.1 and 1-2 into a date. The read stops on such a cell ("type it as text"): start the entry with an apostrophe ('10%). Do not rename or delete the builder's sheets or columns; the read stops if one is missing, so nothing is dropped silently. Notes, source flags and owner records the builder does not show are kept from the current JSON.

    A builder pre-filled from a client spec holds the tender's structure only (labels, never rates). Keep it in the tender folder on the GC laptop. More detail: docs\spec_builder_guide.md in the tool folder.

    premium_basis not NET or GROSSthe value
    Age bands overlapping or with duplicate labels; an unknown band set or column setthe set and the block
    A sheet name too long, duplicated, or using a forbidden characterthe sheet
    A product type or regulator not in the registrythe sheet and the value

    Common changes and what they cost

    ChangeBefore the cedant workbook is filledAfter it is filledAfter the template is issued
    Add or remove a plan, TPA block or age band; change the column split or refer cellsRe-run step 1New workbook from step 1; copy the typed values across (step 2 refuses the old one: spec hash mismatch)Re-issue the template; quotes on the old one fail V5
    Add a factor optionRe-run step 1Use a spare row in the existing table (no new workbook needed)The structure hash is unchanged (factor tables are read-only reference); send reinsurers the refreshed Factor Tables sheet
    Add a rider limitRe-run step 1Use a spare row in the existing rider tableWith quotable riders (addons: FILL) it adds a quote cell, so the hash changes: re-issue
    Add a whole factor table or rider familyRe-run step 1New workbook from step 1 (spare rows cannot create a table)Re-issue
    Change Cover text only (deadline, contact, notes)Re-run step 1No effect on the read-backText only; the structure hash is unchanged. Changing tender_id or a sheet name does change it.
    Who does what

    The tool owner writes and maintains the spec; the analyst reviews the blank cedant workbook against the catalogue (step 4 above) before typing. A real tender's spec holds structure only, so it can sit in the tender folder, but it is never shipped in a release.

    12

    Analysing the outputs

    Per run · in runs\<run_id>\ inside the tender folder

    A reading order

    1. Trust the run. In run_manifest.json or the step-4 window: every gate PASS; coverage well above 95%; V3 implied factor near 1.
    2. Check each quote's data quality. V5 flags per option (options\<id>\v5_flags.csv) and the unpriced share in the rate index. Resolve unit errors before you compare.
    3. Headline price. RateIndex TOTAL rows: index per option on the standard mix.
    4. Where the price moves. The same table by product, emirate, TPA and plan; then RateFactors for cell-level patterns.
    5. Riders and benefits. RiderIndex, BenefitDiff and the benefit-adjusted index.
    6. Treaty effect. TreatyFeed per treaty book, then into the treaty tool.
    7. Recommendation. The pack: ranking, criterion points, and how far each weight is from changing the leader.

    1 · Is the run sound?

    • Coverage (gates\coverage_by_status.csv): the share of premium priced, referred or unmatched. A large REFER share means many lives sit in referred cells (for example older ages) that the comparison cannot price.
    • V3 implied factor (gates\V3_premium_reconciliation.csv) = actual written premium ÷ premium rated at the expiring catalogue's default options. It captures co-pay mix, loadings and discounts the catalogue does not hold. Near 1.0 (training: 1.008) means the catalogue explains the written premium. A factor well away from 1 for one segment points at a mapping error, a wrong plan default or a loading pattern worth asking the cedant about. It is reported, never used to adjust the index.

    2 · Data quality of each quote

    • V5 flags: cells outside 0.7 to 1.3 × expiring. A block of flags on one sheet usually means a unit or basis error (monthly instead of annual, gross instead of net, the TPA difference built into the block). Ask the reinsurer before scoring.
    • Unpriced share (RateIndex unpriced_share): the share of lives the quote did not price (blank or referred cells). An option that refers a large share is not comparable on the headline index; the scorecard's UNPRICED_SHARE criterion penalises it.

    3 · The rate index

    index = Σ option premium ÷ Σ expiring premium over the same Merit cells, weighted by lives in force 1.0255 = 2.6% dearer than expiring 0.9923 = 0.8% cheaper
    • Basis. The headline is base + maternity: every option Merit does not carry (co-pay, deductible, pharmacy, annual limit, network option) is held at its reference factor 1.0 on both sides, and maternity is added at each plan's default limit on Merit's maternity-eligible lives. index_base shows the base alone and index_riders the maternity part.
    • Cuts. cut = TOTAL, then product, product × emirate, × TPA, × plan. Look for where a quote is cheap and where it is dear: a quote cheaper overall but dearer on the largest TPA changes the cedant's economics differently from one that is uniformly cheaper.
    • Scenarios. scenario = STANDARD (lives in force at the snapshot date, latest year), WRITTEN_LY (weighted by written life-years) and UWY_MINUS_1 (the previous year's mix). If the ranking changes between scenarios, it depends on the mix. The spread is scored as ROBUSTNESS_SPREAD.
    • Benefit-adjusted. index_benefit_adj divides by the benefit richness ratio, so a dearer quote that also offers richer benefits is credited for them. It equals index when benefits are unchanged.
    • RateFactors gives option rate ÷ expiring rate for every exposure cell. Use filters to see a quote's age curve or gender relativities against expiring.

    4 · Riders and benefits

    • RiderIndex: quoted ÷ expiring rider premium per rider family and limit, on the eligible lives, with the share of limits not quoted. It is reported, not scored, because riders are bought plan by plan.
    • BenefitDiff: each benefit line of each plan, expiring against option value, the direction (RICHER, LEANER, SAME) and its value factor. BenefitFactors rolls these up per plan into a richness ratio, which feeds the benefit-adjusted index.

    5 · Treaty effect

    rate factor = headline index of the treaty book's cells premium change % = (rate factor × (1 − lapse) − 1) × 100 as-if LR = experience LR ÷ rate factor LR adjustment pts = (as-if LR − experience LR) × 100 Training, SUB_X, BOOK_IND_GREEN: 1.025865 × (1 − 0.06) − 1 = −3.57%; 77.00% ÷ 1.025865 = 75.06% → −1.94 pts

    A dearer quote lowers the as-if loss ratio (good for the reinsurer's result, worse for the cedant's price); the lapse term reflects business expected to leave at the new rates. TreatyScenarios.json holds the same figures in the treaty tool's config format, one scenario per option. Add each reinsurer's terms in the treaty tool and compare the treaty results there.

    6 · The recommendation

    CriterionMeasuresBetter
    PRICEHeadline index (STANDARD, TOTAL)lower
    PRICE_BENEFIT_ADJBenefit-adjusted indexlower
    ROBUSTNESS_SPREADMax − min TOTAL index across the three mix scenarioslower
    UNPRICED_SHAREShare of lives the quote did not pricelower
    V5_FLAG_SHAREFlagged rate cells ÷ rate cellslower
    COMMISSIONCommission %higher
    PROFIT_SHAREProfit share %higher
    CORRIDORLoss corridor width (points)lower
    CAPCap %higher
    SHAREShare of the order offered, on an absolute scale (capped at 100%)higher
    • Score. Each criterion is scaled 0 to 100 across the single options (best = 100, worst = 0), multiplied by its weight, and summed: a score out of 100. SHARE is absolute rather than relative.
    • NO_SPREAD. Every option has the same value on that criterion, so its weight adds the same points to everyone and separates no one.
    • Panels. A panel (e.g. 60% lead, 40% follower) takes the lead's rates and terms on every criterion except SHARE, which is the members' combined capacity. Panels are scored alongside single options and can score outside 0 to 100 on SHARE.
    • Nearest ranking flips. For each criterion, the weight at which the leader would change (one at a time, other weights rescaled). A flip close to the current weight means the recommendation is sensitive to that weight: say so when you present it. WeightGrid shows the ranking over a grid of weights.
    Reading the training result

    SUB_Y ranks first (71.5): it is 0.8% cheaper than expiring (0.9923) and wins the 35% price weight outright. SUB_X is 2.6% dearer (1.0255) but offers the higher commission (17.5% against 15%), so the panel led by SUB_X scores between them. The nearest flip is PRICE: if its weight fell from 35% to about 3.7%, the panel would lead. With a flip that far from the current weight, the recommendation is robust to the price weight. All synthetic.

    14

    Glossary

    Spec Builder
    The Excel view of template_spec.json (steps 0a / 0b). The JSON stays the master; the builder is read back into it.
    Expiring catalogue
    The cedant's current rates, factors, riders and benefits, read back from the cedant workbook (work\expiring.json).
    Option
    One reinsurer's quote, read into a catalogue of its own. Its option_id names it in every output.
    Panel
    A lead and followers scored together; followers write at the lead's rates and terms.
    Exposure cell
    A group of Merit lives sharing product, emirate, TPA, plan, age, gender, marital status, member category and maternity eligibility.
    Standard mix
    Lives in force at the snapshot date in the latest underwriting year: the weights of the headline index.
    Cut
    A grouping of cells for the index: product, emirate, TPA, plan.
    Reference option
    The option a base rate assumes (factor 1.0), e.g. nil co-pay.
    Nil base
    The base rate at nil co-pay; co-pay variants are generated from factor tables, never typed.
    TPA factor basis
    Each TPA block holds the rate before the TPA factor; the TPA factor is a separate table.
    Refer cell
    A cell the catalogue does not price (referred to the reinsurer), shown grey.
    Structure hash
    A fingerprint of a template's layout; quotes must carry the issued template's hash.
    Implied factor (V3)
    Written premium ÷ premium rated at the expiring catalogue on the exposure.
    Treaty book
    A part of the portfolio the treaty tool models separately (e.g. individual, SME, compulsory).
    Run manifest
    run_manifest.json: status, gates, versions and input hashes of a run.
    Pricing Workbench release 1.0.0 · guide written from dry runs on 25 and 26 October 2026 with the synthetic training tender. Commands use the py launcher; the step files use Python 3.12 when present.
